newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's July-Feb budget deficit A$8.004 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australia's July-Feb budget deficit A$8.004 bln.

text.p: Australia's headline budget deficit for the eight months to February, the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$8.004 billion, compared with A$9.044 billion a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Wednesday.
The underlying budget deficit for the eight month period was A$11.956 billion, compared with A$14.043 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Revenue growth from July to February was 7.3 percent, compared with estimates in the government's mid-year budget review of 5.8 percent, Fahey said.
Outlays grew 5.2 percent, compared with mid-year budget review projections of 3.8 percent, he said.
Revenue growth was fuelled by a 7.3 percent increase in tax receipts over the corresponding period in 1995/96.
The monthly headline balance for February, which includes asset sales, was a A$1.856 billion deficit, compared with a deficit of A$2.523 billion a year earlier.
The underlying balance for the month was a A$1.796 billion deficit, compared with a A$2.444 billion deficit in February 1996.
The government has forecast an underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 billion in 1996/97.
